subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Constitutional Bodies & Enabling Articles
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Based on Articles 263, 279A, 280 & 338 of the Constitution of India
source_tag: Laxmikanth 7th Edition · Constitution of India Bare Act
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of Constitutional Bodies and their governing Articles:

1. Inter-State Council : Article 263
2. Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council : Article 279A
3. Finance Commission of India : Article 280
4. National Commission for Scheduled Tribes : Article 338A

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation:
All four pairs are correctly matched:
1. Article 263 provides for the establishment of an Inter-State Council by the President.
2. Article 279A was inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 to establish the GST Council.
3. Article 280 mandates the President to constitute a Finance Commission every fifth year.
4. Article 338A was inserted by the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, bifurcating the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (Art 338) and Scheduled Tribes (Art 338A).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity (7th Ed.), Chapters 45 (Finance Commission), 47 (NCST), 54 (Inter-State Council), 55 (GST Council).
elimination_trap: Candidates often misremember whether GST Council is 279A or 269A. Art 269A deals with levy and collection of GST in course of inter-state trade, while 279A creates the Council.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: More than one pair is correct.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: More than two pairs are correct.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: All four pairs are matched, not just three.
option_analysis.D: Correct: All four pairs are exact constitutional provisions.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: President's Rule (Article 356) & S.R. Bommai Jurisprudence
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) 3 SCC 1
source_tag: Supreme Court Landmark Judgments · Laxmikanth Chapter 16
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
A proclamation of President's Rule under Article 356 of the Constitution of India is subject to judicial review by the Supreme Court and High Courts.
Statement-II :
The Court can assess whether relevant objective material existed to justify the proclamation and whether the exercise of power was mala fide or based on wholly extraneous grounds.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: In the landmark S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) case, a 9-judge Constitution Bench held that presidential proclamation under Article 356 is not immune from judicial review (Statement-I). Statement-II explains why and how judicial review operates: the court cannot examine the sufficiency of advice, but it can verify if objective material existed and whether power was exercised mala fide or on extraneous grounds.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 16 Emergency Provisions: Judicial Review of Article 356.
elimination_trap: Aspirants often confuse 38th Amendment (which barred judicial review) with 44th Amendment and Bommai case (which restored full judicial review).

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II provides the constitutional rationale for Statement-I.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Statement-II directly explains the scope and basis of Statement-I.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Delimitation Commission & 84th Constitutional Amendment
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Articles 82 & 170; Delimitation Act, 2002
source_tag: PIB · Ministry of Law & Justice · Laxmikanth Chapter 22
question_text:
With reference to the Delimitation Commission in India, consider the following statements:
1. Orders issued by the Delimitation Commission have the full force of law and cannot be called into question before any court of law.
2. When the orders of the Delimitation Commission are laid before the Lok Sabha or a State Legislative Assembly, they can be modified by a resolution of the House.
3. The 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001 froze the total number of seats in the Lok Sabha on the basis of the 1971 census until the first census taken after the year 2026.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is correct: Under Section 10(2) of the Delimitation Act, orders of the Commission have force of law and cannot be questioned in any court. Statement 2 is incorrect: When laid before Lok Sabha or State Assemblies, the Houses have NO power to effect any modifications whatsoever. Statement 3 is correct: The 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze on Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 census until the first census taken after 2026.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 22 Parliament: Delimitation of Constituencies.
elimination_trap: Statement 2 contains a major trap: Parliament or State Assemblies CANNOT alter or amend Delimitation Commission orders once finalized.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Statement 2 is false.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Statements 1 and 3 are constitutionally and statutorily verified.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC / e-Rupee) vs UPI
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: RBI Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)
source_tag: RBI Concept Note on CBDC · Economic Survey
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
Unlike Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions, transactions settled via Central Bank Digital Currency (e-Rupee) do not involve commercial bank inter-bank settlement risk.
Statement-II :
e-Rupee is a legal tender issued directly by the Reserve Bank of India and constitutes a direct sovereign liability on the central bank's balance sheet rather than a claim on a commercial bank.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: In UPI, money moves between private accounts in commercial banks through an inter-bank settlement system (clearing via NPCI and bank settlement reserves). In contrast, e-Rupee is digital cash—a direct sovereign liability of the RBI under amended Section 22 of the RBI Act. Because the liability is held directly against the central bank, transaction settlement is instant and final, without commercial bank credit or liquidity risk. Statement-II explains Statement-I.
standard_book_ref: RBI Annual Report / Concept Note on CBDC; Indian Economy by Vivek Singh.
elimination_trap: Aspirants often confuse the front-end user app interface (which looks like UPI) with the underlying settlement ledger (which is central bank digital currency).

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II establishes the financial architecture explaining Statement-I.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Statement-II is the exact causal explanation.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Sustainable Agriculture & Climate Smart Technologies
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: ICAR & Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Guidelines
source_tag: PIB · ICAR · Economic Survey Agriculture Chapter
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of sustainable agricultural techniques and their primary agro-ecological benefits:

1. Direct Seeded Rice (DSR) : Significant reduction in methane emissions and up to 25% irrigation water savings
2. System of Rice Intensification (SRI) : Lower plant population with wider spacing and intermittent aerobic soil conditions
3. Bio-decomposer Pusa Capsule : Enzymatic decomposition of paddy straw converting crop residue into organic manure
4. Liquid Nano Urea : 100% replacement of basal soil application of synthetic phosphatic fertilizers

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation: Pairs 1, 2, and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 4 is INCORRECT: Liquid Nano Urea is designed to substitute conventional granular NITROGENOUS (Urea) fertilizers applied as foliar spray during vegetative growth, NOT phosphatic fertilizers (such as DAP or SSP). It reduces nitrogen leaching and volatilization.
standard_book_ref: ICAR Agricultural Research Reports; Kurukshetra / Yojana Agriculture Special; PMF IAS Agriculture.
elimination_trap: Nano Urea replaces Urea (Nitrogen), not Phosphatic fertilizers (DAP). Read nutrient types carefully!

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Three pairs are correct.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Exactly three pairs (1, 2, 3) are accurately matched.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Pair 4 contains the chemical nutrient mismatch.

subject: Environment & Ecology
sub_topic: BBNJ High Seas Treaty & Marine Genetic Resources
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: UNCLOS BBNJ Agreement Text (A/CONF.232/2023/4)
source_tag: UN Division for Ocean Affairs (DOALOS) · InsightsIAS Jan 2026
question_text:
With reference to the High Seas Treaty (Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction - BBNJ Treaty) adopted under UNCLOS, consider the following statements:
1. It applies exclusively to the waters beyond national jurisdiction, including the high seas and the international seabed Area.
2. It establishes a legally binding mechanism for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from Marine Genetic Resources (MGRs).
3. It completely dissolves the International Seabed Authority (ISA) and transfers deep-sea mining regulation to the UN General Assembly.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 1 is correct: The BBNJ treaty covers marine areas beyond national jurisdiction (ABNJ), comprising the high seas (water column) and the Area (seabed, ocean floor, and subsoil beyond continental shelf limits). Statement 2 is correct: Part II mandates equitable benefit-sharing (both monetary and non-monetary) from Marine Genetic Resources. Statement 3 is completely false: BBNJ respects existing legal frameworks and explicitly does NOT undermine the mandate of the International Seabed Authority (ISA) established under Part XI of UNCLOS.
standard_book_ref: UN Division for Ocean Affairs (DOALOS) Text of BBNJ Treaty; PMF IAS Marine Ecology.
elimination_trap: Extreme statement 3: ISA was NOT dissolved. BBNJ operates without prejudice to the competence of existing bodies like ISA and IMO.

option_analysis.A: Incomplete: Statement 2 is a core pillar of the treaty.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are authentic provisions.

subject: Environment & Ecology
sub_topic: Wildlife Sanctuaries & Conservation Corridors in News
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: MoEFCC Project Cheetah / Wildlife Institute of India (WII)
source_tag: PIB MoEFCC · The Hindu Environment Section
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of Wildlife Protected Areas and their ecological significance in recent news:

1. Kuno National Park : First cheetah introduction site in India within Vindhyan dry deciduous forest
2. Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary : Second prepared habitat for African cheetah release located along the Chambal River
3. Dibang Wildlife Sanctuary : High-altitude habitat of Mishmi takin and proposed site for large-scale hydroelectric development
4. Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve : Habitat of the endangered dugong located exclusively along the Gulf of Mannar

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation: Pairs 1, 2, and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 4 is INCORRECT: Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve is located in the southernmost part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (home to the Nicobar megapode, giant robber crab, and saltwater crocodile). The primary dugong habitat in India is the Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay, and Gulf of Kutch, NOT Great Nicobar Island, which is in the Indian Ocean near Sumatra, thousands of kilometers from the Gulf of Mannar.
standard_book_ref: PMF IAS Environment: Protected Area Network of India; WII Reports on Project Cheetah.
elimination_trap: Pair 4 pairs Great Nicobar with Gulf of Mannar, which are geographically distinct.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Three pairs are correct.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Exactly three pairs (1, 2, 3) are true.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) & Himalayan Geomorphology
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) GLOF Guidelines
source_tag: NDMA Disaster Management Guidelines · NCERT Physical Geography
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
Moraine-dammed glacial lakes in the Eastern Himalayas are significantly more susceptible to catastrophic Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) than lakes in the Western Himalayas.
Statement-II :
The Eastern Himalayas receive intense orographic precipitation from the Bay of Bengal branch of the Southwest Monsoon, combined with higher glacier retreat rates and weaker lateral moraines composed of unconsolidated till.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: Geomorphological studies (NDMA and Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology) highlight that the Eastern Himalayas (e.g., Sikkim, Bhutan) face higher GLOF hazards (such as the South Lhonak lake breach in Teesta basin in 2023) because they experience intense summer monsoon rainfall, higher temperatures, faster glacier melting, and weaker moraine dams composed of poorly sorted loose glacial till. Statement-II accurately provides the physical and meteorological reasons for Statement-I.
standard_book_ref: NDMA Guidelines on Management of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods; D.R. Khullar Geography.
elimination_trap: Glacial lakes are held by loose moraines, not solid bedrock. Heavy rain or avalanches easily breach them.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II provides the direct physical explanation.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Statement-II is the exact causal explanation.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Statement-I is an empirical fact.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Critical Maritime Straits & Global Trade Chokepoints
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: International Maritime Organization (IMO) Navigation Channels
source_tag: Oxford Atlas of the World · NCERT Class XI Geography
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of International Maritime Straits and the water bodies they connect:

1. Bab-el-Mandeb Strait : Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden
2. Strait of Hormuz : Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman
3. Strait of Malacca : Andaman Sea and the South China Sea
4. Bosporus Strait : Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation:
All four pairs are correctly matched:
1. Bab-el-Mandeb ("Gate of Tears") connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden (chokepoint near Djibouti and Yemen).
2. Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea.
3. Strait of Malacca connects the Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean) to the South China Sea (Pacific Ocean).
4. Bosporus Strait bifurcates Istanbul, connecting the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography; Orient BlackSwan / Oxford Student Atlas.
elimination_trap: Aspirants often confuse Dardanelles (Marmara to Aegean) with Bosporus (Black Sea to Marmara). Both are Turkish Straits.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: All pairs are correct.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: All four pairs are matched, not just three.
option_analysis.D: Correct: All four pairs are geographically exact.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Generative AI & Large Language Models (LLM Architecture)
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: MeitY National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence & IEEE AI Architectures
source_tag: MeitY Reports · IEEE Computer Society · Science & Technology Ravi P. Agrahari
question_text:
With reference to Large Language Models (LLMs) and Transformer neural network architectures, consider the following statements:
1. The "Self-Attention" mechanism allows the neural network to weigh the contextual significance of words in a sentence regardless of their positional distance.
2. Transformers process input tokens sequentially one by one, making training times significantly slower than earlier Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs).
3. "AI Hallucination" refers to instances where the model generates plausible-sounding but factually incorrect or ungrounded assertions with high confidence.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is correct: In the foundational 2017 Transformer architecture ("Attention Is All You Need"), self-attention allows the model to calculate relationship weights between all words in parallel across long distances. Statement 2 is incorrect: Unlike RNNs which processed text sequentially and suffered from vanishing gradients, Transformers process entire input sequences in PARALLEL, which is the breakthrough that enabled massive scalability on GPUs. Statement 3 is correct: AI hallucination is the generation of statistically coherent but factually false outputs.
standard_book_ref: MeitY National AI Strategy; Science & Technology by Ravi P. Agrahari.
elimination_trap: Statement 2 reverses technological history: Transformers are fast because they process in PARALLEL, replacing slow sequential RNNs.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Statement 2 is false.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Statements 1 and 3 are scientifically accurate.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Semiconductor Fabrication: Gallium Nitride (GaN) vs Silicon
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) Technology Roadmap
source_tag: PIB ISM · Ministry of Electronics & IT (MeitY)
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
Gallium Nitride (GaN) and Silicon Carbide (SiC) semiconductors are increasingly replacing traditional Silicon in fast electric vehicle chargers and renewable energy inverters.
Statement-II :
GaN and SiC possess a much wider electronic bandgap than Silicon, allowing them to withstand higher operating voltages, frequencies, and temperatures with significantly lower power loss.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: Wide bandgap (WBG) semiconductors like Gallium Nitride (GaN - ~3.4 eV) and Silicon Carbide (SiC - ~3.2 eV) have much larger energy bandgaps than Silicon (1.1 eV). This material property enables devices to operate at higher electric fields, higher switching speeds, and much higher thermal loads, dramatically shrinking device size and heat generation in EV chargers and power electronics. Statement-II provides the exact solid-state physics foundation explaining Statement-I.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Physics, Chapter 14 Semiconductor Electronics; ISM Whitepapers.
elimination_trap: Silicon is the legacy material; GaN and SiC are the high-efficiency Wide Bandgap alternatives.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II explains Statement-I.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Statement-II is the direct explanation.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Statement-I is an industrial reality.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Ancient & Early Medieval Maritime Trading Ports
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Coastal Excavation Reports
source_tag: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part I · Upinder Singh Ancient History
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of ancient Indian ports and their geographic coastal locations:

1. Muziris (Pattanam) : Malabar Coast (ancient Chera kingdom)
2. Arikamedu : Coromandel Coast (Indo-Roman trading station near Puducherry)
3. Sopara (Shurparaka) : Konkan Coast (Western Maharashtra)
4. Tamralipti : Bay of Bengal deltaic coast (ancient Bengal port for trade with Southeast Asia)

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation:
All four pairs are correctly matched:
1. Muziris (Pattanam in Kerala) was the bustling port of the Chera dynasty mentioned in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea and Sangam poems.
2. Arikamedu on the Coromandel coast was excavated by Mortimer Wheeler, yielding Roman amphorae and Arretine ware.
3. Sopara in Palghar district of Maharashtra was a major western port since Mauryan times (Ashokan edict discovered here).
4. Tamralipti (Tamluk in West Bengal) was the premier eastern port from which Buddhist pilgrims (Faxian, Xuanzang) and merchants sailed to Sri Lanka and Suvarnabhumi.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History Part I; Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India.
elimination_trap: Tamralipti is eastern; Sopara and Muziris are western; Arikamedu is southeastern.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: All pairs are correct.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: All four pairs are matched, not just three.
option_analysis.D: Correct: All four pairs are historically and geographically verified.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Temple Architecture: Vesara Style & Hoysala Temples (UNESCO)
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Archaeological Survey of India / UNESCO World Heritage Dossier
source_tag: Nitin Singhania Art & Culture · NCERT An Introduction to Indian Art
question_text:
With reference to the architectural style of the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site), consider the following statements:
1. The Hoysala temples belong to the Vesara hybrid style, synthesizing elements of both Dravida and Nagara traditions.
2. They are characterized by a stellate (star-shaped) ground plan elevated on a wide raised terrace (jagati).
3. Soft chloritic schist (soapstone) was used as the primary building material, enabling intricate and deeply undercut filigree carvings.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: All three statements are correct: Hoysala temples (such as Belur, Halebidu, and Somanathapura in Karnataka) represent the pinnacle of the Vesara style (hybrid of Nagara and Dravida). The ground plan is typically stellate (star-shaped) with multiple shrines (trikuta or vimana) resting on a raised platform (jagati). They were carved out of soft soapstone (chloritic schist), which allowed master sculptors like Mallitamma and Dasoja to carve miniature sculptural friezes with astonishing filigree detail.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI An Introduction to Indian Art Part 1; Nitin Singhania Indian Art and Culture Chapter 1 Temple Architecture.
elimination_trap: Hard granite was used by the Cholas (Brihadisvara), but soapstone was the hallmark of Hoysala architecture.

option_analysis.A: Incomplete: Statement 3 is also historically true.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are all authentic.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Judicial Independence & Collegium System
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (NJAC Judgment) (2016) 5 SCC 1
source_tag: Laxmikanth Chapter 26 Supreme Court · Indian Express Explained
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
The Supreme Court of India struck down the 99th Constitutional Amendment Act and the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) Act as unconstitutional.
Statement-II :
The primacy of the judiciary in judicial appointments is part of the basic structure of the Constitution to protect the independence of the judiciary from executive interference.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: In the Fourth Judges Case (2015), a 5-judge Constitution Bench struck down the 99th Amendment and NJAC Act (Statement-I). The majority ruled that judicial independence is a fundamental facet of the basic structure of the Constitution, and executive participation with veto powers compromised this independence. Thus, Statement-II directly explains Statement-I.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 26 Supreme Court: NJAC & Basic Structure.
elimination_trap: Statement-II is the exact constitutional premise of the NJAC judgment.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II is the judicial reasoning for Statement-I.
option_analysis.B: Incorrect: Statement-II is the direct causal explanation.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Constitutional Amendments & Key Reforms
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Bare Act Amendments 101st to 106th
source_tag: Ministry of Law and Justice Gazette · Laxmikanth Chapter 10
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of Constitutional Amendment Acts and their primary objectives:

1. 101st Amendment Act : Introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST)
2. 102nd Amendment Act : Constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)
3. 103rd Amendment Act : 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)
4. 104th Amendment Act : Complete abolition of reservation for Scheduled Castes in legislative assemblies

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation: Pairs 1, 2, and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 4 is INCORRECT: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2020 EXTENDED the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for an additional ten years (until 2030), while ending the nomination of Anglo-Indians. It did NOT abolish SC reservations.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 10 Amendment of the Constitution.
elimination_trap: 104th Amendment abolished Anglo-Indian nomination, but prolonged SC/ST reservation.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Exactly three pairs (1, 2, 3) are true.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: PESA Act, 1996 & Tribal Gram Sabhas
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 Section 4
source_tag: Ministry of Panchayati Raj · PESA Act 1996 Text
question_text:
Under the Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA), which of the following powers are mandatorily vested in the Gram Sabha in Fifth Schedule areas?
1. Mandatory prior consultation before acquiring land in the Scheduled Areas for development projects.
2. Mandatory recommendation prior to granting prospecting licence or mining lease for minor minerals.
3. The power to enforce prohibition or to regulate or restrict the sale and consumption of any intoxicant.
4. Complete power to override and veto any Act of Parliament relating to defence and national security.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct: Section 4 of PESA Act explicitly mandates Gram Sabha consultation/recommendation for land acquisition, minor minerals leases, ownership of minor forest produce, and enforcement of prohibition. Statement 4 is completely false: Gram Sabhas have no authority to veto Acts of Parliament on national security.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 38 Panchayati Raj: PESA Act 1996.
elimination_trap: Extreme statement 4: Village bodies cannot veto national defense statutes.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Statement 4 is false.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are statutory provisions under Section 4.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) in India
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022 & Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) Rules
source_tag: BEE Ministry of Power · PIB Carbon Markets
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
The Government of India established a domestic compliance Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) to create a market-based incentive for industrial decarbonization.
Statement-II :
Under the CCTS, obligated entities that reduce their greenhouse gas emissions intensity beyond designated government benchmarks are awarded tradable Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs).

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: Under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022, the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) formulated the CCTS (Statement-I). The economic mechanism is a cap-and-trade system where entities exceeding emission reduction targets earn Carbon Credit Certificates, which can be sold on power exchanges to entities that fall short (Statement-II). Statement-II explains Statement-I.
standard_book_ref: Economic Survey Climate Change & Energy Chapter; Ramesh Singh Indian Economy.
elimination_trap: CCCs are market-tradable assets; Statement-II describes the exact cap-and-trade transmission.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II provides the economic mechanism explaining Statement-I.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Types of Foreign Capital & Investment Vehicles
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: FEMA Regulations & RBI Balance of Payments Manual
source_tag: RBI Master Directions · NCERT Macroeconomics
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of foreign investment types and their regulatory attributes in India:

1. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) : Investment of 10% or more in the equity capital of a listed Indian company
2. Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) : Short-term liquid investment in marketable securities without direct management control
3. External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) : Commercial loans raised by eligible resident entities from recognized non-resident lenders
4. Masala Bonds : Foreign currency-denominated debt instruments issued exclusively in the London Stock Exchange

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation: Pairs 1, 2, and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 4 is INCORRECT: Masala Bonds are RUPEE-DENOMINATED bonds issued overseas in international markets. The defining feature of Masala Bonds is that the currency exchange risk is borne by the FOREIGN INVESTOR, not the Indian issuer. They are not foreign currency-denominated.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Macroeconomics, Chapter 6; Ramesh Singh Indian Economy.
elimination_trap: Masala bonds are RUPEE-denominated bonds overseas, insulating Indian borrowers from rupee depreciation.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Exactly three pairs (1, 2, 3) are true.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Pair 4 incorrectly states foreign-currency denominated.

subject: Environment & Ecology
sub_topic: Blue Carbon Ecosystems vs Terrestrial Forests
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: IPCC Special Report on the Ocean and Cryosphere in a Changing Climate (SROCC)
source_tag: UNEP Blue Carbon Reports · PMF IAS Environment
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
Coastal blue carbon ecosystems like mangrove forests and seagrass meadows can sequester and bury carbon per unit area up to ten times faster than terrestrial tropical rainforests.
Statement-II :
Waterlogged coastal saline soils lack oxygen, which drastically slows down the microbial decomposition of organic matter, allowing carbon to remain trapped in sediments for millennia.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: Coastal wetlands (mangroves, salt marshes, seagrass beds) store vast amounts of "Blue Carbon" in deep sediments (Statement-I). In terrestrial forests, dead biomass rapidly decomposes into CO2 in aerobic soils. In coastal wetlands, tidal waterlogging creates anoxic (oxygen-depleted) conditions, preventing aerobic bacteria from breaking down organic carbon (Statement-II). Statement-II is the exact biogeochemical explanation for Statement-I.
standard_book_ref: PMF IAS Environment (Blue Carbon Chapter); Shankar IAS Environment.
elimination_trap: Soil anoxia is the key mechanism preserving carbon in marine coastal sediments.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II provides the biogeochemical mechanism.

subject: Environment & Ecology
sub_topic: Biological Invasions & Invasive Alien Flora in India
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Botanical Survey of India (BSI) Invasive Alien Species of India Report
source_tag: BSI Reports · The Hindu Science & Environment
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of Invasive Alien Plant Species and their ecological consequences in India:

1. Prosopis juliflora : Depletion of native grasses and invasion of Banni grasslands in Gujarat
2. Eichhornia crassipes (Water Hyacinth) : Choking of freshwater waterbodies causing deoxygenation ("Terror of Bengal")
3. Senna spectabilis : Threat to native deciduous vegetation in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (Wayanad)
4. Parthenium hysterophorus (Congress Grass) : Invasive plant introduced deliberately for coastal sand dune stabilization

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation: Pairs 1, 2, and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 4 is INCORRECT: Parthenium hysterophorus was accidentally imported into India as a contaminant in wheat consignments (under the US PL-480 scheme in the 1950s), NOT introduced deliberately for sand dune stabilization. (Prosopis juliflora was introduced for firewood/greening).
standard_book_ref: PMF IAS Environment: Invasive Species; NCERT Class XII Biology Ecology.
elimination_trap: Parthenium was an accidental contaminant in wheat imports, causing toxic allergies and crop loss.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Pairs 1, 2, and 3 are historically and ecologically verified.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) & Monsoon Dynamics
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: India Meteorological Department (IMD) Monsoon Monograph
source_tag: IMD Monographs · NCERT Physical Geography
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
The eastward passage of an active Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) convective wave over the tropical Indian Ocean during summer can trigger a sudden revival of rainfall during a monsoon break.
Statement-II :
The active phase of MJO brings deep anomalous convective cloudiness, enhanced upward air motion, and low-level moisture convergence over the equatorial Indian Ocean.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: Unlike stationary ENSO phenomena, the MJO is an eastward-moving intra-seasonal tropical atmospheric wave (30–60 day periodicity). When its enhanced convective phase enters the Indian Ocean, low-level convergence and rising air revitalize the Indian Summer Monsoon, breaking monsoon dry spells (Statement-I). Statement-II accurately provides the atmospheric physics explaining Statement-I.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Chapter 4 Climate; IMD Climatology.
elimination_trap: MJO moves EASTWARD across the equator, unlike Rossby waves which propagate westward.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II directly explains Statement-I.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Global Oceans: Trenches & Oceanic Features
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: NOAA Bathymetric Atlas & NCERT Class XI
source_tag: NCERT Fundamentals of Physical Geography Chapter 13
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of Oceanic Deep Trenches and the oceans in which they are located:

1. Mariana Trench : Pacific Ocean
2. Java (Sunda) Trench : Indian Ocean
3. Puerto Rico Trench : Atlantic Ocean
4. Diamantina Trench : Arctic Ocean

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation: Pairs 1, 2, and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 4 is INCORRECT: The Diamantina Trench (Diamantina Fracture Zone) is located in the southeastern INDIAN OCEAN (southwest of Australia), NOT in the Arctic Ocean (the deepest point in Arctic Ocean is Molloy Deep).
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Chapter 13 Water (Oceans).
elimination_trap: Java Trench and Diamantina Fracture Zone are both in the Indian Ocean.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect.
option_analysis.C: Correct: Exactly three pairs (1, 2, 3) are true.
option_analysis.D: Incorrect: Diamantina is in Indian Ocean.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: CRISPR Base Editing vs Prime Editing Precision
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Nature Biotechnology Gene Editing Frontiers
source_tag: Nature Biotechnology · Ravi P. Agrahari Science & Technology
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
CRISPR Base Editing and Prime Editing are considered significantly safer therapeutic gene editing techniques than conventional CRISPR-Cas9 for treating human genetic diseases like sickle cell anemia.
Statement-II :
Unlike classic Cas9 nuclease which creates double-stranded DNA breaks (DSBs) that trigger random insertions and deletions, Base and Prime editors perform chemical nucleotide conversions without cutting both strands of the DNA double helix.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: Classic CRISPR-Cas9 acts as molecular scissors creating double-stranded breaks (DSBs), which frequently trigger unguided mutations (indels) or chromosomal translocations. Base editing (converting C->T or A->G directly) and Prime editing (search-and-replace using reverse transcriptase) avoid double-stranded breaks by nicking only one strand, dramatically reducing off-target toxicity (Statement-II). Statement-II explains Statement-I.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Biology, Chapter 11 Biotechnology: Principles and Processes; Nature Biotechnology.
elimination_trap: Double-strand breaks cause genotoxic risks; avoiding DSBs is the defining leap in precision gene editing.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II directly explains Statement-I.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) & WHO Priority Pathogens
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List & National Action Plan on AMR (NAP-AMR)
source_tag: WHO Global AMR Surveillance System (GLASS) · ICMR AMR Network
question_text:
With reference to Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR), consider the following statements:
1. Colistin is regarded as a reserve, last-resort antibiotic for multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacterial infections.
2. Horizontal Gene Transfer (via conjugation, transformation, or transduction) allows resistance genes to spread rapidly between different bacterial species.
3. The excessive use of antibiotics in poultry and livestock farming has zero impact on human antimicrobial resistance because veterinary drugs cannot enter the food chain.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 1 is correct: Colistin is a critical last-resort polymyxin antibiotic. Statement 2 is correct: Horizontal Gene Transfer allows mobile genetic elements (plasmids with mcr-1 genes) to transfer resistance across species. Statement 3 is completely false: The One Health approach shows that antibiotic misuse as growth promoters in livestock contaminates meat, manure, and water bodies, creating resistant superbugs that directly infect humans.
standard_book_ref: WHO Priority Pathogens List; ICMR National Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use.
elimination_trap: Extreme statement 3: "zero impact" is medically false; animal antibiotics drive human AMR.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect: Statement 3 is false.
option_analysis.B: Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are scientific facts.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Bhakti Saints & Philosophical Traditions
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History Part II Chapter 6
source_tag: NCERT Themes in Indian History Part II · Nitin Singhania Art & Culture
question_text:
Consider the following pairs of Bhakti Philosophers and their philosophical doctrines:

1. Shankara : Advaita (Absolute Non-Dualism)
2. Ramanuja : Vishishtadvaita (Qualified Non-Dualism)
3. Madhvacharya : Dvaita (Dualism)
4. Vallabhacharya : Shuddhadvaita (Pure Non-Dualism)

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
explanation:
All four pairs are correctly matched:
1. Adi Shankara (8th century) propounded Advaita Vedanta (Brahman alone is real, the world is Maya).
2. Ramanuja (11th century) expounded Vishishtadvaita (Brahman is qualified by attributes; soul is distinct yet part of God).
3. Madhvacharya (13th century) preached Dvaita (complete eternal distinction between God, individual souls, and matter).
4. Vallabhacharya (15th century) founded Shuddhadvaita and the Pushtimarg tradition of Krishna devotion.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Themes in Indian History Part II; Nitin Singhania Indian Art & Culture.
elimination_trap: All four are the classic Vedantic Darshanas of ancient and medieval India.

option_analysis.A: Incorrect.
option_analysis.C: Incorrect: All four pairs are matched, not just three.
option_analysis.D: Correct: All four pairs are exact philosophical traditions.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Vaikom Satyagraha (1924) Centenary & Temple Entry
upsc_official_key: UPSC Standard Benchmark: Bipan Chandra India's Struggle for Independence Chapter 17
source_tag: Bipan Chandra · Spectrum Modern History
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
Statement-I :
The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924–1925) in the princely state of Travancore marked a major milestone in the Indian freedom struggle for social justice.
Statement-II :
It was a non-violent mass movement launched to secure the right of lower-caste citizens (such as Ezhavas and Pulayas) to walk on the public roads surrounding the Vaikom Mahadeva Temple.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
explanation: Option A is correct: Vaikom Satyagraha began in March 1924 led by T.K. Madhavan, K.P. Kesava Menon, and K. Kelappan, supported by E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar) and Mahatma Gandhi. It was specifically fought against the cruel practice of "unapproachability" to establish the right of oppressed castes to access public temple roads (Statement-II). Statement-II directly explains Statement-I.
standard_book_ref: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence; Spectrum Modern India.
elimination_trap: It was initially for access to public ROADS around the temple, which paved the way for the Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936.

option_analysis.A: Correct: Both statements are true and Statement-II describes the historical movement explaining Statement-I.
